text:
sara: Quick heads-up — reproduced a tool-calling failure when smart-routing falls back to a quantized variant.

sara: Scenario: gold-tier requests routed us-east -> primary model (model-ggml-v3) hits capacity, router falls back to model-quant-v2 which has shorter context handling and different tokenizer. Tool-call payloads come back 400s with "unrecognized tool signature".

mike_h: :eyes: do we have a repro script? can you paste minimal request + response?

sara: here — posting condensed logs:
```
POST /v1/chat
model: model-ggml-v3 -> fallback: model-quant-v2
payload: { \"input\": \"run_tool:calc(2+2)\", \"tools\": [{\"name\":\"calc\",\"signature\":\"(expr)->number\"}] }
response 400: { \"error\": \"tool_signature_mismatch\", \"detail\": \"expected tuple, got str\" }
```

jules: hmm that smells like tokenizer/param ordering differences. quant-v2's tokenizer maps parentheses differently when subword-splitting occurs, so tool payload is mutated. Do we do any canonicalization before routing? :thinking_face: 

liam_dev: We currently do no canonicalization in the router. The fallback path is model-variant-opaque: router just swaps model name and proxies bytes. If tokenization differs, the model sees different token ids. We assumed tool-calling parity across variants — that was naive.

anika_pm: From product/console perspective this is a UX issue. Customers on gold expect seamless fallback. We need to decide tradeoffs: restrict fallback to variants flagged as "tool-compatible" or attempt on-the-fly normalization. Thoughts?

mike_h: Engineering options:
- Conservative: enforce compatibility matrix (router checks `variant.meta.compatibility.tool_calling == true`) before fallback. Drop-through to next region/tier otherwise.
- Aggressive: add a canonicalizer step to normalize tool payloads (escape sequences, explicit JSON wrappers) before routing.
- Hybrid: do compat checks + best-effort canonicalization and telemetry to measure failures.

jules: Compat matrix sounds easiest and safest. We already have a per-variant metadata store. Need fields: tokenizer_name, tokenizer_version, max_context_tokens, tool_calling_parity (boolean), kv_cache_behavior. Router can consult it during policy eval.

sara: downside: reduces available fallbacks -> more latency/5xx during capacity spikes for premium customers. But avoids surprising tool failures. Could we have a console flag per-customer: "allowUnsafeFallbacks"? Customer sets opt-in with clear risk note.

anika_pm: Yes — expose in console rollout UI: toggle with tooltip "May fallback to faster but not tool-compatible variants". Telemetry: surface incidents in dashboard and auto-trigger alert to SEs.

liam_dev: Implementation plan proposal:
1) Extend variant metadata with tokenizer and tool_parity tags.
2) Router policy evaluator consults metadata and fallback policy (tier + region) to build candidate set.
3) If no parity-compatible candidate in region, try cross-region if latency budget permits, otherwise respect customer's unsafe toggle.
4) Emit structured telemetry event `fallback.decision` with fields (customer_id, from_model, to_model, reason, latency_budget_ms, parity_ok).

mike_h: Also add unit/integration tests that simulate tokenization mismatch and tool-call payloads. Add a small fuzz harness that verifies tool signature survives round-trip for every compatible variant.

sara: I'm happy to pick up prototyping the metadata + router check. Will spike canonicalizer separately if we need it.

opsbot: @channel rollout-bot: feature flag "variant_tool_parity_check" scheduled for canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC. :rocket:

anika_pm: Thanks — I'll draft the console UX copy and add a telemetry dashboard mock. Can we add a low-severity smoke alert if fallback.tool_signature_mismatch > 0.1% of requests in 5m?

liam_dev: sure, add alert config: `fallback.tool_signature_mismatch.rate > 0.001` over 5m. Also track per-region and per-tier.

jules: wfm. I'll update the compatibility docs and add a short section on tokenizer/versioning policy (how we bump tokenizer version and release notes).

sara: OK pushing PR for router gating + telemetry today. tagging @mike_h @jules for review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
